title: The product comparison maps
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$,
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and $k=\overline{k_0}$, the finite-field datum of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension
$E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a chosen $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$.
Use the geometric operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum] and
its six-functor structure [def-sf-datum], with the constructible domains,
compact-support base change and exceptional adjunction supplied by
[thm-weil-six-operations], restricted to $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$
of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] at every coefficient stage, as in the
source. These restrictions are justified by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]:
(i), (ii), (iv), (v) give finite-stage pullback, tensor, compact-support
image and exceptional inverse-image preservation, and (vii) identifies
the integral finite-Tor category with the derived-complete $D^b_c$
category and supplies preservation and coefficient passage to the field
stages. At field coefficients $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by definition. In
particular, $Rf_!$ is the concrete compact-support functor of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] at finite coefficients and
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] at the other stages;
$Rf^!$ and its adjunction counit are the specified constructible
exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. All
uses of (A1) and (A2) of [def-sf-datum] below refer to these same geometric
functors and their specified units, counits and exchange maps, on the
stated domains. At $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ this is the
exceptional-admissibility datum of [def-trf-admissibility]; that definition
is not being extended to the other coefficient stages. No unrestricted
ambient exceptional adjoint is assumed.

For $i=1,2$, let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be separated finite-type $k$-morphisms
between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, put $f=f_1\times_k f_2$, and let
$L_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,\Lambda)$ and $B_i\in D^b_{ctf}(X_i,\Lambda)$.
All products in this definition without a displayed relative base are
over $k$. For $K_i$ on $Z_i$, write
$K_1\boxtimes K_2=Lr_1^*K_1\otimes^L_\Lambda Lr_2^*K_2$ on
$Z_1\times_k Z_2$, where $r_i$ are the projections; pullback, tensor and
internal Hom are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].
Integral pullback and tensor are completed, and field coefficients use
rationalization and common finite coefficient fields as in that node.

1. **(i)** Define the $!$-Künneth isomorphism
$$
\mathrm{Ku}_!:Rf_!(B_1\boxtimes B_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf_{1!}B_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}B_2
$$
as follows. Set $T=Y_1\times_kY_2$ with projections $t_i:T\to Y_i$,
$U=X_1\times_kY_2$, $V=Y_1\times_kX_2$,
$u=f_1\times\operatorname{id}_{Y_2}:U\to T$ and
$v=\operatorname{id}_{Y_1}\times f_2:V\to T$.
Write $a_1:U\to X_1$ and $a_2:V\to X_2$ for the other projections,
$W=U\times_TV$, $p:W\to U$, $q:W\to V$, and $h=up=vq$.
The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $W$ with
$X_1\times_kX_2$ over $T$; under this identification $h=f$ and
$a_1p=r_1$, $a_2q=r_2$. Put $K=La_1^*B_1$, $H=La_2^*B_2$.
The pullback-composition and monoidal comparisons of
[lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], together with the defining
identifications of the external products, identify
$$
Lp^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lq^*H
\cong Lr_1^*B_1\otimes^L_\Lambda Lr_2^*B_2
=B_1\boxtimes B_2.
$$
Apply [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] to $u,v$ over the separated finite-type
base $T$, and to $K,H$. Its target is
$Ru_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rv_!H$.
For each $i$, the square with vertical arrows $u,f_1$ (respectively
$v,f_2$) and horizontal arrows $a_1,t_1$ (respectively $a_2,t_2$) is
Cartesian. Compact-support base change (A2) for these two squares gives
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}:Lt_1^*Rf_{1!}B_1\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_!La_1^*B_1,
\qquad
\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}:Lt_2^*Rf_{2!}B_2\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_!La_2^*B_2.
$$
Compose the relative product isomorphism with
$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,1}^{-1}\otimes^L\operatorname{Ex}_{!,2}^{-1}$.
The resulting target is
$Lt_1^*Rf_{1!}B_1\otimes^L_\Lambda Lt_2^*Rf_{2!}B_2
=Rf_{1!}B_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}B_2$; this composite is $\mathrm{Ku}_!$.
Here $u,v$ are base changes of the separated finite-type maps $f_i$,
and [thm-sf-ctf-stability] supplies the finite-Tor preservation used
for $K,H$, their tensor product, and the compact-support images. Every arrow in this construction is
an isomorphism.

1. **(ii)** Define the exceptional Künneth map
$$
\alpha:Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\longrightarrow
Rf^!(L_1\boxtimes L_2)
$$
to be the exceptional adjoint, under the geometric $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$
of (A1), of the composite
$$
Rf_!\bigl(Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ku}_!}
Rf_{1!}Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}Rf_2^!L_2
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2}
L_1\boxtimes L_2.
$$
Here [thm-sf-ctf-stability] ensures that $Rf_i^!L_i$ and their external
product lie in the domains of (i). The maps
$\varepsilon_i:Rf_{i!}Rf_i^!\to\operatorname{id}$ are the counits
of those same geometric constructible adjunctions. Thus the source of
this adjunction transpose is an object of $D^b_{ctf}(X_1\times_kX_2,\Lambda)$.

1. **(iii)** For $E_i\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_i,\Lambda)$ on the same scheme as
$L_i$, define the external Hom map
$$
\beta:\RHom(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes\RHom(E_2,L_2)
\longrightarrow\RHom(E_1\boxtimes E_2,L_1\boxtimes L_2)
$$
as the tensor–Hom transpose of the two evaluations. Internal Hom lies
in the stated categories by [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (ii), (vii). Explicitly, put
$H_i=\RHom(E_i,L_i)$ and tensor its proposed source with
$E_1\boxtimes E_2$. The signed tensor symmetry and reassociation identify
this tensor product with
$Lt_1^*(H_1\otimes^LE_1)\otimes^LLt_2^*(H_2\otimes^LE_2)$.
Apply $Lt_1^*\mathrm{ev}_1\otimes^LLt_2^*\mathrm{ev}_2$ to obtain
$L_1\boxtimes L_2$, and transpose. The tensor constraints include their
Koszul signs; no invertibility of $\beta$ is assumed.

1. **(iv)** For separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$, write
$a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $p_X,p_Y$ be the projections
of $X\times_kY$. Use $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda_s$ and
$\mathbb D_YN=\RHom(N,\omega_Y)$ of [def-sf-pf], formed with the same
geometric exceptional adjoint and internal Hom. The coefficient unit
has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$; exceptional and internal-Hom preservation
in [thm-sf-ctf-stability] therefore put $\omega_Y$ and $\mathbb D_YN$
in the required finite-Tor categories. For
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, define
$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN
&\xrightarrow{\beta}\RHom\bigl(Lp_Y^*N,M\boxtimes\omega_Y\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\RHom(1,\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y})}
\RHom\bigl(Lp_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $\beta$ uses $(E_1,L_1)=(\Lambda_X,M)$ on $X$ and
$(E_2,L_2)=(N,\omega_Y)$ on $Y$, with the unit identifications
$\RHom(\Lambda_X,M)\cong M$ and $\Lambda_X\boxtimes N\cong Lp_Y^*N$.
The second arrow uses (ii) with $f_1=\operatorname{id}_X$, $f_2=a_Y$,
$L_1=M$, $L_2=\Lambda_s$: its target base is $X\times_ks\cong X$,
which is separated, and its product morphism is $p_X$.

Only $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is built from isomorphisms; invertibility of
$\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\kappa$ is the content of the forward references
[prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth], [prop-trf-external-hom] and
[thm-trf-kunneth-verdier].

blueprint_update.statement:
For $i=1,2$ let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be separated of finite type between
finite-type $k$-schemes, exceptionally admissible in the sense of
[def-trf-admissibility] where $Rf^!$ occurs — which every such morphism is,
no ambient datum being assumed — (with $Rf^!$ the exceptional
inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and $Rf_!$ the
compact-support direct image of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed],
[def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]), put $f=f_1\times f_2$, and let
$L_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$, $B_i\in\Dctf(X_i,\Lambda)$.

1. **(i)** The $!$-Künneth
$\mathrm{Ku}_!:Rf_!(B_1\boxtimes B_2)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_{1!}B_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}B_2$ is [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] for the base
$B=Y_1\times Y_2$, using
$X_1\times X_2=(X_1\times Y_2)\times_B(Y_1\times X_2)$. It is an isomorphism.
1. **(ii)** The *exceptional Künneth*
$\alpha:Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\to Rf^!(L_1\boxtimes L_2)$ is the
exceptional adjoint of
$$
Rf_!\bigl(Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_2^!L_2\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{Ku}_!\ }
Rf_{1!}Rf_1^!L_1\boxtimes Rf_{2!}Rf_2^!L_2
\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon_1\boxtimes\varepsilon_2\ }
L_1\boxtimes L_2 ,
$$
where the $\varepsilon_i$ are the counits of $Rf_{i!}\dashv Rf_i^!$
(axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum]).
1. **(iii)** For $E_i\in\Dctf(Y_i,\Lambda)$, on the same scheme $Y_i$ as
$L_i$, the *external Hom* map
$$
\beta:\RHom(E_1,L_1)\boxtimes\RHom(E_2,L_2)
\longrightarrow\RHom\bigl(E_1\boxtimes E_2,L_1\boxtimes L_2\bigr)
$$
is the tensor–Hom transpose of the two evaluations, with the tensor symmetry
and its Koszul signs.
1. **(iv)** For separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ whose structure
morphism $a_Y$ and product projection
$p_X=\operatorname{id}_X\times a_Y:X\times Y\to X$ satisfy the
exceptional-adjoint admissibility of [def-trf-admissibility] (the inputs
for $\omega_Y$ and $\mathbb D_Y$, for $Rp_X^!$, and for
$\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y}$), for
$M\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ and $N\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$, with
$p_X,p_Y$ the projections of $X\times Y$, and with the Verdier dual
$\mathbb D_Y$ and dualizing complex $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda$ of [def-sf-pf], the
*Künneth–Verdier* map is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\kappa_{M,N}:M\boxtimes\mathbb D_YN
&\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,M\boxtimes\omega_Y\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ \RHom(1,\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_Y})\ }
\RHom\bigl(p_Y^*N,Rp_X^!M\bigr),
\end{aligned}
$$
using the unit identifications $\RHom(\Lambda_X,M)=M$ and
$\Lambda_X\boxtimes N=p_Y^*N$; here $\beta$ is applied to the pairs
$(E_1,L_1)=(\Lambda_X,M)$ on $X$ and $(E_2,L_2)=(N,\omega_Y)$ on $Y$.

Only $\mathrm{Ku}_!$ is built from isomorphisms; invertibility of
$\alpha,\beta,\kappa$ is the content of [prop-trf-exceptional-kunneth], [prop-trf-external-hom]
and [thm-trf-kunneth-verdier].
